finding: ITEM-4's readability upgrade stops one step short of the question its own comment asks ("it asks whether the path can be READ"): the new guard is `!canon.is_file()`, so a prompt_file naming a REAL but non-UTF8 file (a .png/.pdf shipped in the bundle) validates GREEN at install AND at the runner's pre-dispatch re-validate, then fails the RUN in load_raw_prompt with `read prompt_file 'x': stream did not contain valid UTF-8`. That is exactly DESIGN §1's non-negotiable ('a definition the validator reports GREEN must not fail at run for a prompt-configuration reason') and exactly the shape of the design's row-4 directory cell, just a different unreadable-ness. TEST-1's bundle contains no non-UTF8 file so the matrix cannot see it.

Asymmetry the shared rule introduces: `prompt: ""` is now refused because an empty prompt is degenerate (PromptSource::Missing -> Err), but `prompt_file:` pointing at a ZERO-BYTE file yields PromptSource::File -> Ok("") -> resolve_prompt -> `ChatMessage::user("")` at dispatch.rs:176 with NO emptiness guard, while the validator is GREEN. DESIGN §1's second half ('a definition the validator reports RED must not quietly succeed at run with a degenerate prompt') is upheld for the inline half and left open for the file half — the same degenerate empty LLM call the inline fix exists to prevent. TEST-1's bundle has only a non-empty real.md, so the matrix has no empty-file row.

The named acceptance test asserts only AGREEMENT (`prompt_findings.is_empty() == run.is_ok()`), never the DIRECTION DESIGN §1 chose. Mutation tried: drop the emptiness filter on the inline half of prompt_source (`let inline = prompt.as_deref();`, validate.rs:1086) — i.e. adopt dispatch's old rule instead of validate's. Then ('',file) is Both/Err (agree) and ('',None) is Inline("")/Ok("") (agree): all 60 cells still pass, yet DESIGN's 'Direction' section explicitly forbids that resolution (it re-creates the false red on the state the builder's own remedy produces) and row 2 requires that state to be RED. NOT caught by TEST-1; caught only by TEST-2/TEST-3 (validate.rs:1794/1794+), which are not the stated acceptance proof.

TEST-1 claims 'the whole authorable state space' and its PROMPT_CODES list includes WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_UNSAFE and WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_ESCAPE, but the `files` array carries no '..'/absolute/escaping path — precisely the rows where the asserted implication FAILS today. check_prompt_files pushes UNSAFE and `continue`s (validate.rs:1150-1157) while load_raw_prompt still does a raw `bundle_root.join(rel)` with no path-safety check, so `prompt_file: prompts/../prompts/real.md` is validator-RED and run-OK. Adding that one string to `files` turns TEST-1 red. The shared rule therefore does NOT unify path-safety, only presence/emptiness; the claim of exhaustiveness is overstated.

ITEM-7's permanent guard is not reached by the enforced gate. `npm run gate:ui` (the repo's stated UI exit condition per CLAUDE.md) runs the visual layer with an explicit allow-list, `CFG.visualSpecs` = [layout, form-label-starvation, states, overlays, chat-collapse-borders] (sdk/packages/gallery/scripts/gate-ui.mjs:184-186). `input-group-overflow.spec.ts` was not added, although the sibling the PLAN says it mirrors (form-label-starvation.spec.ts) IS listed. So the spec that is supposed to make the defect non-recurring never runs in the gate engineers are told to run before pushing UI work; it runs only via `npm run test:visual` or the CI workflow.

The one CI job that runs the whole visual config unfiltered is path-gated on `src-app/ui/**` / package.json / the workflow file. The guarded component lives in the `sdk` submodule, so the change class that both CAUSED this defect and DELIVERED its fix — an sdk submodule-pointer bump touching only the `sdk` gitlink — does not trigger visual-tests.yml. Combined with the gate:ui allow-list omission, a future kit regression in inputGroupAddonVariants can land with neither guard executing.

Scope beyond DESIGN §3 as written. §2 names only the `inline-end` addon ('inputGroupAddonVariants' inline-end variant is order-last pr-2 has-[>button]:mr-[-0.3rem]…') and §3 says 'Any other kit spacing … out of scope. This branch fixes the two recorded residuals and nothing else.' The change also restyles the `inline-start` variant (pl-2 -> ps-2, plus new has-[>button]:ps-1 / has-[>kbd]:ps-1.5), altering start-side spacing by ~0.8px and changing LTR/RTL behaviour of a variant the design never named. Defensible (identical negative-margin defect, declared in PLAN ITEM-6) but it is more than §3 authorised.

ITEM-5 changed the client rule but left the authoritative doc block above it stating the SUPERSEDED backend rule: 'MIRRORS validate.rs (~681-691), the sole authority on this rule: … has_file = prompt_file.is_some()'. That is the exact expression the diff deleted from validate.rs, and the line reference is now stale (prompt_source lives at 1082). A reader reconciling client and backend is pointed at the pre-fix contract, which is the drift the shared-rule item exists to prevent.

The directory case reuses WORKFLOW_PROMPT_FILE_MISSING (ITEM-4 says deliberately, to avoid new copy), but the author-facing copy keyed to that code (ui/src/modules/workflow/components/builder/validationCopy.ts:104-105) reads 'This step points at a prompt file that isn't in the workflow — add the file, or type the prompt in directly.' For `prompt_file: prompts/adir` the file IS in the workflow, and adding it is not the remedy — the author is told something false about the new verdict.

REJECTED: candidate 'the agent kind never reaches the shared rule'. agent_dispatch.rs:1101 calls dispatch::resolve_prompt, which calls load_raw_prompt (dispatch.rs:92), so all three kinds named by FIX_ROUND-8 (llm, llm_map, agent) run through prompt_source on the production path.

REJECTED: candidate 'a validator-RED definition can still run (UNSAFE/ESCAPE paths)'. The runner re-parses and re-runs validate_for_install against the real extracted bundle before dispatch at spawn (runner.rs:1248) and resume (runner.rs:1552), and every prompt finding is Severity::Error (ValidationError::at, validate.rs:460-473), which validate_for_install blocks. So no RED definition reaches load_raw_prompt in production; the UNSAFE gap is a test-scope defect, not a reachable behaviour.

REJECTED: candidate '§3 out-of-scope whitespace cell was changed'. prompt_source filters with is_empty(), never trim(); TEST-2 pins Inline("   ") alone and Both for "   " beside a file, and the client's promptSuppliedByFile deliberately returns true for a whitespace PATH. The `prompt: "   "` cell behaves exactly as before on both sides.

REJECTED: candidate 'the kit fix is not actually reaching the app / the visual spec is vacuous'. @ziee/kit resolves to source (sdk/packages/kit/package.json exports './src/index.ts'), and measuring the live gallery at 390px and 1280px gives 2 input-groups, both carrying an inline-end addon with a >button child, scrollWidth-clientWidth = 0 and the addon's right edge 1px INSIDE the group. Re-injecting margin-inline-end:-0.3rem restores exactly the recorded 5px overflow / 3.8px bleed at both widths, so the spec's falsifiability control does fire.

REJECTED: candidate 'TEST-1 does not pin the prompt_file emptiness rule'. It does not (mutating prompt_file_ref to drop the filter keeps every cell agreeing: prompt_file "" then canonicalises to the bundle dir, trips the new !is_file() branch, and the run errors with 'Is a directory' — agreement holds), but that mutation does not violate INV-1 as stated, and the specific verdict (PROMPT_MISSING, which ITEM-5's client mirror depends on) is pinned by TEST-2, TEST-3 and the /validate-def integration TEST-4.

REJECTED: candidate 'prompt: "x" beside prompt_file: "" silently flipped from RED to GREEN'. It did (old has_file = is_some() made it WORKFLOW_PROMPT_BOTH), but under the canonical rule DESIGN §1 chose it is Inline at BOTH ends — validator green, run resolves the inline prompt — so the two sides agree and INV-1 holds. It is a consequence of the chosen direction, not a violation.
